body:
## Goal

From **any installed browser** it must be possible to do a **full import** or a **cross import** into **any browser instance Browser Commander controls**, in JS, Rust and Python with identical options, and from the CLI (reachable through command-stream). A fresh, clean profile stays the default; import is opt-in.

- **Full import**: same-engine clone of everything the browser stores, so the controlled instance is as close as possible to the user's real one (Chrome → controlled Chrome, Firefox → controlled Firefox, Safari → controlled WebKit where possible).
- **Cross import**: translate data between engines (Safari → Chromium, Chrome → Firefox, Firefox → WebKit, ...), every data class the target can hold.

## What exists today (0.21.2)

- Sources: `chrome`, `chromium`, `brave`, `edge`, `firefox` (`SUPPORTED_COOKIE_BROWSERS`, `migration/index.js`).
- Target: a **Chromium** profile only (Firefox data is converted to Chrome formats, `firefoxBookmarksToChrome`). Controlled Firefox/WebKit instances cannot receive an import.
- Data classes: `cookies`, `bookmarks`, `history`, `passwords`, `preferences`, `extensions`.

## Missing

### Sources
- **Safari** and Safari Technology Preview: cookies from `~/Library/Containers/com.apple.Safari/Data/Library/Cookies/Cookies.binarycookies` (fallback `~/Library/Cookies/Cookies.binarycookies`; documented, unencrypted format), `Bookmarks.plist`, `History.db`, LocalStorage/IndexedDB under the Safari container. Passwords live in the iCloud Keychain and cannot be read directly: offer the documented path (Safari / Passwords app "Export Passwords" CSV, then import that CSV) instead of silently skipping.
- Other Chromium browsers: **Opera, Opera GX, Vivaldi, Arc, Yandex, Chrome Beta/Dev/Canary, Edge Beta/Dev**, any custom `userDataDir`. The format is the Chromium one; mostly profile-root paths plus each browser's Keychain/DPAPI/libsecret key name.
- Firefox forks: **LibreWolf, Waterfox, Zen, Floorp, Firefox Developer Edition / Nightly** (profiles.ini locations).
- **Default browser**: `browser: 'default'` / `'auto'` resolves the system default (existing `system-browser.js` detection) and, for a `domains` request, falls back to other installed browsers that hold cookies for those domains, reporting which one was used.

### Targets
- Import into a controlled **Firefox** instance (cookies.sqlite / via BiDi or the CDP-less path, places.sqlite, logins.json + key4.db re-encryption, prefs.js, extensions where signing allows).
- Import into a controlled **WebKit** instance (Playwright WebKit: cookies via `context.addCookies`, storage state for localStorage/IndexedDB; persistent-context files where supported).
- Same-engine **full clone** mode for every engine: copy the whole profile (snapshot of a locked profile, as `attach snapshot` does), re-keying encrypted stores for the controlled instance, so nothing is lost by translation.

### Data classes
Add to the existing six:
- `localStorage`, `indexedDB`, `sessionStorage` (many sites keep their sign-in there, not only in cookies)
- `autofill` (addresses; payment cards only behind an explicit flag)
- `searchEngines`, `siteSettings`/permissions, `openTabs`/sessions, `downloads` history, `readingList`, client certificates where the OS allows
- **Passkeys**: not exportable from iCloud Keychain / Google Password Manager / Windows Hello by design. Report them as a skipped class with that reason, and document the supported path (sign in once in the controlled instance with the platform passkey; the persistent profile keeps the session).

### Behaviour
- Every class reports `migrated` / `skipped` (with reason) / `warnings` per source and target, as today.
- `domains` filtering applies to every class that is per-site (cookies, storage, passwords, history, permissions).
- Clear errors for OS protection: macOS Full Disk Access for Safari's container (`EPERM`; name the app that needs it and offer `x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_AllFiles`), Keychain prompts for Chromium Safe Storage keys, locked profiles (use the snapshot path).
- `cookies sources --domain <d>` / `profile sources`: which installed browsers and profiles hold data for a domain (names and counts only, never values), so callers can ask "import your github.com sign-in from Safari?" before reading anything.
- A source × target × data-class support matrix in the README, generated from the code and checked in CI, the same in all three languages.

### Tests
Fixture profiles for every source family (Chromium, Firefox, Safari `.binarycookies`/plist/sqlite) and round-trip tests into every target engine; parity tests across JS, Rust and Python; the EPERM and locked-profile paths.

Consumer: link-foundation/package-registry-manager#26 (reuse an existing registry/GitHub sign-in so crates.io/npm/PyPI publishing needs no manual login).


## Linked implementation work

The reopening comment permits splitting remaining requirements into linked issues.
PR #116 implements Safari/Safari Technology Preview **cookie** sources for the
existing Chromium import target, plus source/default/custom discovery and Safari
cookie Full Disk Access guidance. It does not close this tracking issue.

- [ ] #117 — Safari non-cookie sources (plist/sqlite/password CSV), modern named profiles and WebsiteDataStore paths.
- [ ] #118 — Firefox/WebKit import targets and same-engine full profile clones.
- [ ] #119 — Storage, autofill, settings, sessions, downloads, reading list, certificates and explicit passkey reporting; per-site domains filtering.
- [ ] #120 — Remaining protection/lock diagnostics, discovery and the generated source × target × data-class support matrix with native parity/round-trip tests.

Keep #114 open until the complete import goal and the acceptance criteria in these linked issues have shipped.
title: Full and cross import from every installed browser (incl. Safari, Opera, Vivaldi, Arc, Firefox forks) into every controlled engine (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit)
